mission: Inside the breach zone, each character's response reveals their truth through character-differentiated unweaving sensations (per D4). Ben experiences the Force as a conversation he cannot fully hear — multiple voices, each partial. Sera works against the missing second blade. Kael moves through the zone with the economy of someone who is finally home. Desh holds the operational frame while grief-without-an-object lands on his body. Per D7 Component A, Torin does NOT smile in the breach — he walks into the worst of it, stops, stands there a long time, and when he turns his face is unreadable to Ben, to Sera, to the reader. Something happened in him; we do not yet know what. Per B1 R08a, the array-dependency lands felt-and-understood: Desh's chrono-drift reading and Ben's sensing converge without dialogue into the specific conclusion that Veranthos is the only place Veraine's ritual can complete. Per B2 seed, Ben feels the anchors' multiplicative coupling — their presences drawing harder on each other than last time — without naming it. Cascade-acceleration is planted as body-knowledge, to be paid at Ch 18 and Ch 21.
why_now: The unwoven zone strips performance off everyone in it. Each character's honest register surfaces when the Force can no longer mediate. Per D7, Torin's register here is withheld rather than exposed — his direction is not the answer the midpoint delivers; the answer is the embodied experience of full unweaving, plus two pieces of load-bearing knowledge that travel through Ben's body rather than through exposition.
conflict: Sera fights to hold discipline against the missing second blade. Kael navigates the zone with unexpected ease. Desh reports environmental data the way he always reports environmental data while grief that does not know its object lands on him. Torin's Force presence changes in the deepest part of the breach and Ben cannot read which way it changed. The withheld answer is the most pressure-loaded ambiguity in the book so far.
turning_point: Ben's body understands two things before his mind does. First: the zone's shape is anchored to a geographical specific, and the only place Veraine's ritual can complete is Veranthos. Second: the surviving anchors are drawing harder on each other than they were the last time he sensed them. Neither of these lands as a sentence; both land as felt-fact. Meanwhile, Torin stops at the worst of the breach and stands unreadable.
opening_hook: Inside the unwoven zone: the Force arrives in pieces, each voice partial. Sera's hands clench. Kael moves like someone whose feet know the ground. Torin walks toward the worst of it and does not come back for a long time
closing_hook: They leave the zone. The Weave snaps back — the relief is immediate and physical. Ben looks at Torin and cannot read what is in him. He does not know what Ben is looking for. Ben does not know what he is looking at
emotional_trajectory: Group distress differentiated by training -> Ben's body absorbing two load-bearing facts without language -> Torin's unreadable return -> held ambiguity on departure

stakes.personal: Ben's pattern-recognition pressurising without the vocabulary to name what he is reading — per D1 Trauma Lie under test, his capacity to judge whose Force-reading is trustworthy is specifically the skill the midpoint asks him to use without any of the usual instruments
stakes.interpersonal: The group has been inside full unweaving together. Something happened to Torin. No one has a name for what they saw or did not see.
stakes.external: If the wound opens fully, this is what the galaxy feels. Veranthos is the specific site. Cascade is accelerating.

setting: Breach Zone — deep inside the unwoven area, then retreat to the perimeter
sensory_details: The Force as multiple voices speaking at once, each partial — Ben assembling nothing; Sera's bilateral muscle memory meeting no reciprocal pressure and compensating every beat late; Kael's breathing steady in a place where everyone else's pattern has broken; Desh's face registering a sadness without an object, noted in his tone but not in his speech; Torin walking into the dead centre of the breach and staying there; the Weave snapping back on exit with a relief Ben feels behind his sternum; Torin's face on turning, absolutely still, absolutely unreadable
canon_elements_needed: Force wound phenomenology in full-unweaving register
Geographical anchoring of Force rituals in Legends metaphysics
action_beats: Sera's hands clench and her body braces against a pressure that does not arrive — her Force-lock training running without its reciprocal
Kael moves through the zone with the economy of someone who is finally home; his breathing does not change
Ben reaches for the Force and gets multiple partial voices, each a fraction; he stops assembling

Desh's chrono-drift readings line up in Ben's peripheral vision with what Ben's body is sensing about the zone's shape — Veranthos as the only completion site resolves as felt-fact, not as a spoken conclusion
Ben's attention registers the surviving anchors drawing harder on each other than before — a multiplicative coupling he cannot put into words, planted for later
Torin walks into the worst of it, stops, stands there a long time
Torin turns; his face is unreadable; the group absorbs the silence and steps out of the zone
promises_planted: The array-dependency fact (plants Ch 13, pays Ch 14 onward, ultimate Ch 25-26)
Cascade-acceleration as tactical constraint (plants Ch 13, reinforces Ch 18, pays Ch 21)
notes: Per D7 Component A, Torin does NOT smile in the breach — this was the loudest telegraph in the original blueprint and it has been relocated per the D7 restructure. Here he is unreadable. The withholding is the beat. Per D7 Component B, the narrator does not over-signal Torin's direction past Ben's perception; Ben's reading of Torin is rendered as *Ben's reading*, and the narrator does not correct for it. Per D4 character-differentiated unweaving, use the full sensory vocabulary: Ben (conversation he cannot fully hear), Sera (missing second blade), Kael (finally home), Torin (weightlessness his body keeps mistaking for flow-state — but this sensation is held in Torin and not shown to Ben directly), Desh (grief without an object that does not lift until leaving the zone). Ben perceives only what Ben can perceive. Per B1 R08a, the array-dependency fact lands as felt-and-understood: Desh's chrono-drift reading correlates with Ben's sensing of the zone's shape, and the specific conclusion — Veranthos is the only completion site — resolves in Ben's body before it resolves in speech. Do not narrate it aloud. Per B2 cascade-acceleration seed, Ben feels the anchors' multiplicative coupling without naming it. The fact is planted for Ch 18 reinforcement and Ch 21 payoff. No character articulates cascade-acceleration in this chapter. Per R11, Ben does not, in this scene, articulate the Jacen parallel in interiority. The recognition is a flash; the word 'Jacen' belongs to Ch 18 per R13's single explicit-naming budget. Write Ben's recognition as a body-response (a cold that lives below the sternum, a step he does not take toward Torin) and trust the reader to hold the echo. Maetha's 'replaces you' should surface once in Ben's memory, fragment only, not in quotation. Per D4 concept-vs-sensation rule, no 'it was as if the Force had—' metaphors; the Force does not have 'as if'; it has 'is' or 'is not.' Per D3, use the Weave terminology consistently — 'the Weave snaps back' on exit, etc. Voice: Bujold-warmth interior allowed in interior passages; Stover-density constrained and earned; Zahn-tight for the procedural frame around the interior beats. One extended Stover-permitted passage allowed in this scene. Primary anchor: Stover (the book's most interior high-stakes Force passage); supporting anchor: Bujold (Ben's self-aware interior register), Zahn (clean frame). Anti-patterns: (a) Torin does NOT smile; (b) no character names the Jacen parallel; (c) neither R08a nor cascade-acceleration is spoken aloud — both land as felt-fact.
